forbiddenMatchPairs.note: Pre-registered limitation: the deterministic near-match rule does not flag leading-zero variants. This pair must NOT appear as a proposal; the limitation is reported in the evaluation, not patched silently.

expectedFindings.note: Before the alias decision there is no quantity-mismatch finding because RM-7702 has no consumed links at all (both issues sit on variant codes; GapEngine requires received>0 and consumed>0). After confirming the RM-7702/RM-77O2 alias and regenerating, the canonical consumed total is 160 kg -> mismatch 320 vs 160 is expected. The RM-07702 chain (120 kg) stays outside forever unless a human manually resolves that variant, which the deterministic rule never proposes.

postAliasSuspect.stateCountsNote: Audit history: original pre-registered value was Candidate:0. On 2026-10-19 a pre-execution mechanics review changed it to Candidate:1, assuming the old RM-77O2->PB-2026-1205-C candidate link would be traversed backwards into the post-alias scope. That assumption was wrong: the first execution of this scenario (run eval-dev-20261019-d) showed the engine resolves the variant's candidate edge onto the canonical RM-7702 node and dedupes it against the confirmed canonical raw_to_batch edge, so the post-alias scope honestly counts 0 Candidate edges (and the trace summary states '3 confirmed, 0 pending review'). The value was reverted to the original pre-registered Candidate:0; this history is preserved for audit.
